question:
Direction: In the following questions, choose the word opposite in meaning to the given word.

Restriction
solution:
The correct answer is 'Sanction'.

Key Points

  • The word 'Restriction' is a noun and it refers to a limiting condition or measure, especially a legal one.
    • For example, 'The US president urged other countries to follow the trade restrictions with Russia.'
  • The marked option 'Sanction' in one denotation means approval or permission, especially formal or legal.
    • For example, 'They tried to get official sanction for the plans.'
  • So, we can see that 'Sanction' can function as the opposite word of 'Restriction' in meaning.

Hence, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

  • Embargo ⇒ an official ban on trade or other commercial activity with a particular country.
  • Ban ⇒ officially or legally prohibit.
  • Proscription ⇒ the action of forbidding something. It may also refer to condemnation or denunciation of something.

Confusion Points

  • The word 'Sanction' is an example of a contronym or Janus word: a word having two meanings that contradict one another, depending on the context. In one denotation, 'Sanction' may mean formal and official permission, in another, it may refer to an official order, such as the stopping of trade, that is taken against a country in order to make it obey international law.
    • As here no other option is opposite in meaning to the given word, we need to choose 'Sanction' as the correct answer.
  • Other examples of Contronyms are: Cleave, Fast, Lease, Literally, Oversight, Quantum, Table, Transparent, Weather etc.

question:
What is the antonym of the word given below?

Ambiguous
solution:
The correct answer is Clear. 

Key Points

Ambiguous: open to more than one interpretation; not having one obvious meaning

Clear: easy to perceive, understand, or interpret

Thus we can see that Ambiguous and Clear are antonyms. 

Additional Information

The meaning of the other words:

  • Uncertain: not knowing what to do or believe, or not able to decide about something
  • Obscure: not clear and difficult to understand
  • Vague: not clearly expressed, known, described, or decided
     

Ambiguous, Uncertain, Obscure and Vague are all synonyms or near-synonyms.

question:
Directions: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Social class formed by people whose employment and income are insecure.
solution:
The correct answer is Precariat.

Key Points

  • Word meaning is the use of one word in place of a wordy phrase in order to make the sentence structure clearer. The meaning, with the replacement of the phrase remains identical while the sentence becomes shorter.
    • For eg: Atheist: The one who does not believe in God.
  • The word most suitable for the given group of words 'Social class formed by people whose employment and income are insecure' is 'Precariat' (ऐसे लोगों द्वारा गठित सामाजिक वर्ग जिनका रोजगार और आय असुरक्षित है). 
    • Ex: Her recent work has concerned the emerging precariat class.

​Hence, option 4 is the correct answer.

Additional Information 

  • Elite: a social group that is thought to be the best or the most important because of its power, money, intelligence.
  • Upper Class: refers to a group of individuals who occupy the highest place and status in society.
  • Nouveau Riche: somebody who has become rich recently and spends a lot of money to show how rich they are.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in bold.
We'd better watch our step and not give him any excuse to harass us further.
solution:
The correct answer is: Option 4.

Key Points

  • The word "harass" means to trouble, torment, or bully someone persistently. (परेशान करना)

  • "Intimidate" refers to making someone feel frightened or overawed, especially in order to make them do what one wants. (डराना)

question:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.

Were you ever taught how to behave?
options: Did anyone ever teaching you how to behave?
Did anyone ever taught you how to behave?
Does anyone ever teach you how to behave?
Did anyone ever teach you how to behave?
solution:
The correct answer is 'Did anyone ever teach you how to behave?'

Key Points

  • The given sentence is in the Passive Voice. As per the given question we have to change the sentence into Active Form. 
  • The process of transformation of these kinds of sentences as follows:
    • Here, 'were taught' will be changed into 'did teach'. (Passive to Active)
    • The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject. 
    • Example:
      • Were you frightened by the strange noise? (Passive Voice)
      • Did the strange noise frighten you? (Active Voice)
  • Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 3. 
    ​

Correct Sentence: Did anyone ever teach you how to behave? 

Additional Information

  • When what/which is used as a subject of a sentence, it is changed into by what/which. 
  • Example: 
    • What makes you happy in your life? (Active Voice)
    • By what are you made happy in your life? (Passive Voice)

question:
Choose the appropriate indirect speech for the given sentence:

"I am here to bury Caesar, not to praise him" said Mark Anthony
options: Mark Anthony remarked that he was there to bury Caesar, not to praise him.
Mark Anthony remarked that he is here to bury Caesar and not to praise him.
Mark Anthony was here to bury Caesar and not to praise him.
Mark Anthony said I am here to bury Caesar and not to praise him.
solution:
The correct answer is 'Mark Anthony remarked that he was there to bury Caesar, not to praise him.'

Key Points

  • When the reporting verb (said) of direct speech is in past tense then all the present tenses (am) are changed to the corresponding past tense in indirect speech.
    • So the correct sentence is: Mark Anthony remarked that he was there to bury Caesar, not to praise him.

question:
Direction: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Efficacy
solution:
The correct answer is "Incompetence".

Key Points 

  • Efficacy means 'the ability of something like a drug or a medical treatment to bring about the results that are wanted (क्षमता, प्रभावोत्पादकता)'.
    • Example: Covaxin booster shot enhances efficacy against Delta.
  • Marked option 'Incompetence' means 'inability to do something successfully; ineptitude (अयोग्‍यता, असमर्थता, अक्षमता)'.
    • Example: The government's lack of planning and incompetence is responsible for the oxygen crisis.
  • It is clear that Efficacy and 'Incompetence' are opposite in meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is option 1. 

Additional Information 

  • Effectiveness means the degree to which something is successful in producing the desired result; success (प्रभावोत्‍पादकता). 
  • Productiveness means having the quality or power of producing something, especially in abundance (उत्पादकता, उत्पादन क्षमता). 
  • Puissance means great power, influence, or prowess (बड़ी ताकत, बड़ा प्रभाव होना, कौशल, साहस).

question:
Select the option that is the correct direct speech of the given sentence.

She advised him to use a softer tone and milder words if he wanted people to help him.
options: She told him, "If you wanted to help you, use a softer tone and milder words."
She told him, "If you want people to help you, use a softer tone and milder words."
She told him, "Use a softer tone and milder words and people will listen to you."
She told him, "Mind you, if you want people to help you, you must use a softer tone and milder words."
solution:
The correct answer is option 2, i.e., She told him, "If you want people to help you, use a softer tone and milder words."

Key Points

  •  Since the sentence is an advice, the reported speech uses the verb 'advised'. In direct speech, the general verb 'told' is appropriate here.
  •  So, the direct speech sentence would begin with 'She told him'.
  •  The sentence uses the conjunction 'if', which is generally used in the beginning to join two sentences.
  •  Then, the second sentence starting with 'if' would become the first.
  •  Rule: When converting sentences to direct from reported speech; the third person pronouns become first/second person pronouns.
  •  Here, it is an advice that is given by her to him, so we use the second person pronoun 'you' instead of 'he' and 'him'.
  •  Also, simple past tense from reported speech would become a simple present tense in direct speech. So, the verb 'wanted' becomes 'want'.

Thus, the direct sentence is: She told him, "If you want people to help you, use a softer tone and milder words."

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
Can you compose an inspiring poem?
options: Can an inspiring poem be composed?
An inspiring poem can be composed by you.
Can an inspiring poem be composed by you?
Can an inspiring poem by you composed?
solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
  • In the active voice, the sentence is: "Can you compose an inspiring poem?"
  • To convert to passive voice: Place the object "an inspiring poem" at the beginning.
  • Change the active verb form "compose" to "be composed" (passive infinitive form).
  • Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "you."
  • Ensure the question structure remains intact by placing the auxiliary verb "can" at the beginning.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Correct Sentence: "Can an inspiring poem be composed by you?"
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "Can an inspiring poem be composed?" – This sentence is in passive voice but lacks the agent "by you."
  • Option 2: "An inspiring poem can be composed by you." – This is a passive voice sentence but not in question form.
  • Option 4: "Can an inspiring poem by you composed?" – This sentence is grammatically incorrect.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
The strain caused by / the difficulties and anxieties / were more than / she could bear.
solution:
​The correct answer is 'were more than'.

Key Points

  • The erroneous part is were more than.
  • In the given sentence, the subject is strain. 
  • The phrase '... caused by the difficulties and anxieties ...' comes between the subject (strain) and the verb (were)
  • When a phrase comes between the subject and the verb, the verb still agrees with the subject, not the noun or pronoun in the phrase following the subject of the sentence.
  • Thus, the sentence can be corrected by using the singular verb was to maintain subject-verb agreement. 

Correct sentence - The strain caused by / the difficulties and anxieties / was more than / she could bear.

question:

solution:
Here the erroneous part is 'I have scarcely no qualms​.'

Key Points    

  • The error lies in the part 'I have scarcely no qualms​' of the sentence.

  • Therefore, "any" will be used instead of ‘no’.

Correct sentence: I have scarcely any qualms about the rights and wrongs of my doing.

question:
Choose the appropriate prepositions for the given sentence:

He was ________ prison ________ a crime that he had not committed.
solution:
The correct answer is "in, for".

Key Points

  • The complete sentence is:
    • He was in prison for a crime that he had not committed.
  • ​In and for are prepositions.
  • Duration is indicated by "for".
  • The word "in" denotes the beginning. 

Additional Information

  • Prepositions are words or phrases that are used in front of a noun, pronoun, or noun phrase to indicate time, place, location, direction, or spatial relationships, or to introduce an item.
  • Words like "in", "at", "on", "of", and "to" are a few examples of prepositions.
  • English prepositions contain a lot of idioms.

question:

question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

The professor said, “You must learn these words regularly.
options: The professor said I should learn these words regularly.
The professor said that I had to learn those words regularly.
The professor said that I must learn these words regularly.
The professor said that you had to learn these words regularly.
solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 2'.

Key Points

  • To convert it into indirect speech, we need to make the necessary changes:
  • Change the pronoun "you" to the appropriate pronoun based on the context.
  • Since the professor said the statement, we can assume that the person being addressed is the person reporting the statement.
  • Therefore, "you" changes to "I" in the indirect form.
  • Change the verb form from "must" to a verb form that reflects indirect speech. In this case, "must" changes to "had to" in the indirect form.
  • Add the conjunction "that" to introduce the reported statement.

Therefore, the correct sentence is: The professor said that I had to learn those words regularly.

question:

  • By referring to the above explanation, it can be concluded that hardships should be the appropriate option to be chosen for filling the blank.

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.
